taxonomyNote: NatureServe uses Urile pelagicus (genus split from Phalacrocorax after Kennedy & Spencer 2014); Canadian government pages still list Phalacrocorax pelagicus.
fieldMarks: Smallest Pacific-coast cormorant, 61-81 cm, with a small head and thin bill
Very glossy overall; dark red facial skin hard to see
Breeding adults show white flank patches
Immatures plain dark brown, best identified by shape
behavior: Dives from the surface to at least 120 ft, taking fish near the bottom over rocky reefs
Forages singly; groups perch on rocks with wings held out to dry
Nests in colonies on narrow near-vertical cliff ledges; male flashes white flank patches in display
Groaning and hissing calls at colonies; shy and hard to approach
habitat: Rocky coasts, bays and sounds, usually close to shore, near deep water at cliff bases.
range: Pacific coast from the Bering Strait and Alaska south to Baja California, including British Columbia; northernmost breeders move south in winter.

lookalikes.name: Other Pacific-coast cormorants
lookalikes.howToTell: Larger with a bigger head and thicker bill.
